text:
A: Hello! Oh, hiya. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah, yeah, all good. Callum. Sorry about the music, there's a nail bar under my flat.
A: Oh, I can just hear a bit of bass. I'm Claire. Don't worry, I've had worse. My son used to play drum and bass at two in the morning.
B: Proper. How old is he?
A: Joe's twenty, he's at uni in Glasgow. You actually remind me of him a bit, from your photo. The clothes rail especially. He's got a rail exactly like that, I don't think he's ever hung anything on it.
B: Ha! Nah, mine's organised chaos, you get me. Everything on there's from Depop, though. Got a jacket last week for fifteen quid.
A: Fifteen quid! I love a charity shop. I go round Otley and Ilkley on my days off. Erm, so what do you do, Callum?
B: I'm at uni as well, media and comms, second year. Plus I do events stuff on the side, production, warehouse parties.
A: Oh, that sounds fun. Joe would love that. Is it fun, or is it just carrying things?
B: Bit of both, ngl. Mostly carrying speakers at four in the morning. But it's contacts, innit. That's what counts in that world.
A: That's true, I suppose. What sort of thing do you want to do after?
B: Music marketing, campaigns, that kind of thing. Or start my own night with mates.
A: Ooh, a club night. What would you call it?
B: Erm... haven't got that far, to be honest. Working on it.
A: Ha, that's the hardest bit. I'd spend six months on the name and never book the venue. I've got that poster too, haven't I, in your photo? The film, Oldboy?
B: Yeah, Oldboy, Korean. The bloke I just talked to, Martin, he'd seen it as well, which I wasn't expecting.
A: The engineer one? He looked very sensible. Reminded me of my husband.
B: He was alright, actually. Knows his books. Do you watch Korean stuff?
A: Not really films, but I've been on a big Korean food kick. I've got a jar of gochujang in the fridge and I'm learning a bit of Korean on an app, on and off. Mostly off. I tried a kimchi stew last week and it went a bit wrong, sort of, it was more like a sad orange soup.
B: Nah, see, the thing is, you need the old kimchi for that, the proper sour stuff. Fresh kimchi doesn't work.
A: Is that it? Oh, that makes sense actually. I used it straight out the jar. Do you cook, then?
B: Erm, not really. I eat, mostly. There's a decent Korean place in Peckham, though, I'll be honest.
A: Ha! That's very Joe. He only rings when he needs money or wants to know how long you cook rice for.
B: Twenty minutes, tell him. Is it boring, being a speech therapist? Sorry, that came out wrong.
A: No, no, it's not boring at all! It's lovely. Little ones who aren't talking yet, and you get down on the floor with a bag of toys and suddenly they say "bus" and you're chuffed for a week.
B: That's actually nice, that.
A: It is. The paperwork's awful, mind, I'm hopeless at it. Do you get your essays done on time?
B: Yeah, no, definitely. Mostly. Kind of.
A: Ha, that's a no, love. Joe says exactly that.
B: Okay, okay, I resubmitted two last year. Don't tell my lecturer—
